Implementation: Centralize EncryptResultV1 Success Responses

Summary

Added the reusable Functions.EncryptSuccessResponseV1 utility and routed all 17 identical non-Slim encrypted success responses through it. The refactor preserves the existing HTTP and encryption behavior without adding dependencies or changing Slim handlers.

Changes

  • Added EncryptSuccessResponseV1(c, rowDatas) to src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Centralized the fixed EncryptResultV1 arguments: success, true, and HTTP 200.
  • Centralized the existing HTTP 500 Internal Server Error response.
  • Replaced each matching handler block with one return statement.
  • Added TestEncryptSuccessResponseV1 using the existing Fiber dependency and Go standard library HTTP testing.

Affected Handlers

  • Bookmarks: ListBookmarks, ListFolderBookmarks
  • Hashtag: SearchHashtagPost
  • MentionPosts: SearchMentioningUser
  • Posts: GetFilterCustom, ListDraftPosts
  • Search: SearchFolderBookmark, SearchHistories, SearchPublishedFolderBookmark
  • Users: CheckPassword, ListAccountStreetView, ListUserAccount, ProfileUser, ProfileUserBySid, SuggestionUserHalf, SuggestionUserMore, UserDetail

Shared files:

  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions_test.go

Resulting Data Flow

  1. A handler builds its existing []interface{} row data.
  2. The handler returns Functions.EncryptSuccessResponseV1(c, rowDatas).
  3. The utility calls EncryptResultV1 with the unchanged success metadata.
  4. An encryption error returns the existing HTTP 500 response.
  5. A successful encryption returns the encrypted JSON payload with HTTP 200.

Test

TestEncryptSuccessResponseV1 sends a request through a minimal Fiber app and verifies:

  • HTTP status 200.
  • Payload statusCode 200.
  • Payload status true.
  • Payload message success.

No fixture layer, mock framework, or table abstraction was added.

Scope Audit

The final scan reported:

  • 17 Functions.EncryptSuccessResponseV1 calls.
  • 11 non-Slim direct EncryptResultV1 calls intentionally retained because their flows differ.

Verification

gofmt -w <changed Go files>
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • The focused Functions utility test passes.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.

Problem

Seventeen non-Slim handlers repeated the same successful EncryptResultV1 response flow: encrypt with fixed success metadata, translate an encryption error into the same HTTP 500 response, then return the encrypted payload with HTTP 200.

Keeping this response plumbing in every handler adds duplication and allows status or error behavior to drift.

Scope

  • Add one reusable Functions.EncryptSuccessResponseV1 utility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Replace all 17 identical non-Slim response blocks with the shared utility.
  • Preserve each handler's existing []interface{} encryption input.
  • Preserve success message, validity flag, response status, error status, and error messages.
  • Add one focused test for the utility's successful HTTP response.
  • Keep all *Slim.go files unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

The utility must preserve the previous behavior:

  • Call EncryptResultV1 with message success, valid status true, and status code 200.
  • Return Internal Server Error through Functions.ErrorResponse with HTTP 500 when encryption returns an error.
  • Return the encrypted map as JSON with HTTP 200 on success.
  • Pass the caller's rowDatas slice through unchanged.

Out of Scope

  • Migrating the 11 non-Slim EncryptResultV1 calls with different assignment, error, or return flows.
  • Migrating duplicated blocks in *Slim.go files.
  • Changing EncryptResultV1, its positional []interface{} contract, or encryption output.
  • Introducing generics, response interfaces, or new dependencies.
  • Changing queries, filters, response data, ordering, or pagination.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Functions.EncryptSuccessResponseV1 exists in the shared Functions package.
  • All 17 identical non-Slim blocks call the shared utility.
  • No identical block remains in non-Slim handlers.
  • The 11 behaviorally different non-Slim calls remain unchanged.
  • No *Slim.go file changes.
  • The utility has a focused success-response test.
  • Changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-08-31. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Encrypt Success Results

Summary

Added the reusable Functions.EncryptSuccessResult utility and routed all 70 identical legacy encryption preparations through it. The refactor changes 70 handlers plus the shared Functions file, removes 280 lines, and adds 77 lines without adding dependencies or changing response behavior.

Changes

  • Added EncryptSuccessResult(data interface{}, lastLogin, encrypt string) string to src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Moved the repeated KeyEncrypt, positional row-data construction, and fixed EncryptResult success arguments into the utility.
  • Replaced every exact three-step caller block with one utility call.
  • Kept caller-specific response envelopes and HTTP returns in their original handlers.
  • Preserved the previous ignored-error behavior instead of introducing a new error contract during the refactor.

Affected Packages

  • Action/V1/Posts: 14 files
  • Action/V1/Users: 11 files
  • Action/V1/Search: 8 files
  • Action/V1/Places: 7 files
  • Action/V1/Bookmarks: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Comments: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Broadcast: 4 files
  • Action/V1/Likes: 3 files
  • Action/V1/Affiliate: 2 files
  • Action/V1/CollectionPost: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Hashtag: 2 files
  • Action/V1/MentionPosts: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Notifications: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Categories: 1 file
  • Utils/Functions: 1 file

Resulting Data Flow

  1. A handler passes its existing response data, last-login value, and encrypt value to Functions.EncryptSuccessResult.
  2. The utility generates the same legacy secret through KeyEncrypt.
  3. The utility builds []interface{}{secret, lastLogin, 0, data}.
  4. The utility calls EncryptResult with success, true, and HTTP 200.
  5. The encrypted string returns to the handler.
  6. The handler builds its unchanged messages, cry, ls, optional e4, and HTTP response.

Scope Audit

The final scan reported:

  • 70 Functions.EncryptSuccessResult calls across 70 handlers.
  • 1 different Recommendations encryption flow intentionally retained.

Verification

gofmt -l <changed Go files>
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All 71 changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Seventy V1 handlers repeated the same encryption preparation flow:

  1. Generate the legacy encryption key with Functions.KeyEncrypt.
  2. Build []interface{}{secret, lastLogin, 0, data}.
  3. Call Functions.EncryptResult with fixed values "success", true, and status code 200.
  4. Ignore both returned errors.

The response envelopes differ by handler, but the encryption input construction and fixed success metadata are identical.

Scope

  • Add one reusable Functions.EncryptSuccessResult(data, lastLogin, encrypt) utility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Replace all 70 exact blocks across 14 Action V1 packages.
  • Keep each caller's response message, envelope, role handling, e4, HTTP status, data selection, and return flow unchanged.
  • Preserve the existing ignored-error behavior for KeyEncrypt and EncryptResult.
  • Keep Support and Slim flows unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

The utility must preserve the previous flow exactly:

  • Call KeyEncrypt(lastLogin, encrypt) and continue with its returned secret while ignoring its error.
  • Build the positional []interface{} input in the same order: secret, last login, zero, and caller data.
  • Call EncryptResult with message success, valid status true, and status code 200.
  • Return the encrypted string while ignoring the encryption error.
  • Leave HTTP response construction in each handler.

Out of Scope

  • Support handlers, which handle EncryptResult errors explicitly.
  • *Slim.go files and sl/V1 encryption flows.
  • EncryptSuccessResponseV1 callers.
  • Recommendations/PopularPosts.go, whose local encryption flow has a different shape.
  • Changing EncryptResult, KeyEncrypt, encryption output, error policy, or response schemas.
  • Consolidating caller-specific response envelopes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Functions.EncryptSuccessResult exists in the shared Functions package.
  • Exactly 70 matching callers use the utility.
  • No matching encText, _ := Functions.EncryptResult(...) block remains in the scoped files.
  • Support, Slim, and the Recommendations outlier remain unchanged.
  • Existing response messages, cry, ls, e4, and HTTP behavior remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-01. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Pagination

Summary

Added the reusable Functions.Pagination utility and routed all 49 identical pagination flows through it. The implementation changes 44 handlers, the shared Functions file, and its test file. It removes 505 lines and adds 87 lines without adding dependencies or changing pagination behavior.

Changes

  • Added Pagination(c *fiber.Ctx, defaultLimit int) (int, int, int) returning page, limit, and offset.
  • Centralized Fiber query parsing, zero-value defaults, and offset calculation.
  • Replaced each exact manual block with one utility call.
  • Used _ for page in handlers that only consume limit and offset.
  • Kept page in 11 flows that expose it later in their response.
  • Added TestPagination for explicit query values and the default path.

Affected Packages

  • Action/V1/Supports: 10 flows
  • Action/V1/Users: 6 flows
  • Action/V1/Bookmarks: 5 flows
  • Action/V1/Posts: 5 flows
  • Action/V1/Search: 5 flows
  • Action/V1/Broadcast: 4 flows
  • Action/V1/Hashtag: 4 flows
  • Action/V1/Places: 4 flows
  • Action/V1/Affiliate: 2 flows
  • Action/V1/Notifications: 2 flows
  • Action/V1/Comments: 1 flow
  • Action/V1/MentionPosts: 1 flow
  • Utils/Functions: utility and test files

Several consolidated Slim files contain more than one migrated handler, so 49 flows map to 44 handler files.

Resulting Data Flow

  1. A handler calls Functions.Pagination(c, defaultLimit).
  2. The utility reads the page and limit query values.
  3. Page zero becomes 1.
  4. Limit zero becomes the caller's supplied default.
  5. Offset is calculated with the original formula.
  6. The handler receives page, limit, and offset, ignoring page when it is not otherwise used.

Test

TestPagination verifies:

  • page=3 and limit=5 return page 3, limit 5, and offset 10.
  • Missing query values with default limit 20 return page 1, limit 20, and offset 0.

No fixture layer, mock framework, or new dependency was added.

Scope Audit

The final scan reported:

  • 49 Functions.Pagination calls.
  • 0 remaining exact manual pagination blocks.
  • Default-limit distribution unchanged: 24/15/4/3/2/1 calls for defaults 20/10/9/2/15/8.
  • 46 changed Go files: 44 handlers, one utility file, and one test file.

Verification

gofmt -l <changed Go files>
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused pagination test passes.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Forty-nine handler flows repeated the same pagination setup:

  1. Read page and limit with Fiber QueryInt.
  2. Default page zero to page 1.
  3. Default limit zero to an endpoint-specific value.
  4. Calculate offset with (page * limit) - limit.

The blocks were identical except for their default limits, which ranged from 2 to 20.

Scope

  • Add one reusable Functions.Pagination(c, defaultLimit) utility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Replace all 49 exact blocks across 44 Action V1 files.
  • Include matching Slim and Support handlers.
  • Preserve every endpoint's existing default limit.
  • Return page, limit, and offset so handlers that expose page metadata keep the same response.
  • Add a focused unit test for explicit and default query values.

Behavior Boundary

The utility must preserve the previous behavior:

  • Read page and limit through c.QueryInt.
  • Replace only zero page values with 1.
  • Replace only zero limit values with the supplied default.
  • Keep negative and other nonzero values unchanged.
  • Calculate offset with the existing formula.
  • Let callers decide whether page is needed in their response.

Default Limits

  • 20: 24 flows
  • 10: 15 flows
  • 9: 4 flows
  • 2: 3 flows
  • 15: 2 flows
  • 8: 1 flow

Out of Scope

  • Changing query parameter names.
  • Adding minimum, maximum, or negative-value validation.
  • Introducing a pagination struct or middleware.
  • Changing database queries, ordering, response schemas, or totals.
  • Migrating pagination code with a different control flow.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Functions.Pagination exists in the shared Functions package.
  • All 49 exact blocks call the utility.
  • No matching manual pagination block remains.
  • All six default-limit values retain their original call counts.
  • Handlers that return page metadata still receive page from the utility.
  • Slim and Support handlers in scope are migrated.
  • Explicit and default query behavior is covered by a focused test.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-01. No commit was created.
